paragraphs.text: Located at 3337 Penn Avenue in Lower Lawrenceville, Lola's Eatery is a brunch spot and cafe founded in December 2019 by owners Max and Zoë Blume. The concept blends Filipino and Mexican culinary influences with house-baked goods such as bagels, donuts, and customized cakes. The name 'LOLA' references both Lower Lawrenceville and the Filipino translation for grandmother.

“LOLA” stands for Lower Lawrenceville, a community that has played a big role in Zoë’s life, “LOLA” also translates to “Grandmother” in the Filipino language. Max’s Filipino and Mexican background brings a unique inspiration to their dishes while the baked delights are fashioned from Zoë’s imagination and nonpareil pastry skill.

In December of 2019, Max and Zoë Blume opened Lola's intending to offer Lawerencevile a brunch spot that offered dishes that not only included Filipino/Mexican influenced dishes but also fresh-baked bagels, customized cakes, delicious donuts, and so many more. Having opened only two months before the pandemic (Covid-19) hit, the married duo had to pivot their plans and make necessary changes to survive the Lockdown.

At Lola's Eatery, our menu is comprised of food that is approachable, creative, and fresh. We take extra care in providing a quality eating experience: making our food with real ingredients, house-made seasonings, sauces + spreads, donuts and bagels fresh daily, made-to-order sandwiches, and partnerships with local vendors.

paragraphs.text: The venue operates a counter-service format where guests place orders before food is delivered to tables. Featured menu items include fresh-baked donuts, ube cinnamon rolls, rosemary bagels, French toast, and savory entrees like adobo fried rice and the 'MR. BATE DACON' (honey wheat bread topped with smashed avocado, glazed bacon, Medjool date, Goat Rodeo goat cheese, herbed oil, and micro-cilantro).
